title: When I read the Bible, it feels like I’m there—witnessing the truth unfold…
paragraphs: When I read the Bible, it feels like I’m there—witnessing the truth unfold…
I imagine standing quietly in Abram’s camp as the desert night settles in. The tents grow still. Lamps begin to glow. Conversations fade into silence.
Years have passed since the promise was spoken.
I watch her gaze drift across the wilderness… as if searching the horizon for something only faith can see.

Waiting has a way of testing the heart.
It stretches hope.
It exposes doubts we try to hide.
Yet somehow the promise still lingers in the quiet air of the camp.
Because God’s promises are not measured by our timelines.
Sometimes the longest seasons of waiting are where the deepest faith is formed.
Standing here as a quiet witness… I realize something.
The delay did not mean God forgot.
He was preparing a miracle that would arrive at the exact moment history needed it.
What promise in my life might still be quietly unfolding… even while I wait?
